summary: Turkey lets most European, Latin American and East Asian passport holders enter visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180, and runs an official eVisa portal (evisa.gov.tr) for nationalities that still need a visa, including a conditional eVisa for travelers holding a valid Schengen, US, UK or Irish visa.

conditionalWaivers.text: Several visa-required nationalities qualify for Turkey's conditional eVisa if they hold a valid visa or residence permit from the US, the UK, Ireland or a Schengen country.

defaultStayWindow.text: Türkiye counts the allowance across a rolling 180-day window: the MFA states the exemption as “90 days in any 180-day period” for nationality after nationality. Leaving and coming back does not start a fresh 90 days — days spent in the previous 180 still count against you. The MFA does not say whether the day you arrive and the day you leave are themselves counted, so we count both.

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement for tourists (it is only mandatory when applying for a residence permit), but medical coverage is strongly recommended — foreigners pay for treatment.

source.name: Turkish MFA — Visa Information For Foreigners

onwardTicket.text: Onward travel is not systematically checked at the border, but airlines and immigration officers may ask for proof of return or onward travel and accommodation.

source.name: Turkish MFA — Visa Information For Foreigners

proofOfFunds.text: There is no published fixed amount, but border officers may ask travelers to show sufficient means of support for the intended stay.

source.name: Turkish MFA — Visa Information For Foreigners

currencyLimits.text: Cash of 10,000 USD or more (or equivalent in other currencies) should be declared when entering or leaving Turkey. Confirm current thresholds with Turkish customs before carrying large sums.

notes: Exporting antiquities, fossils or "old-looking" stones and artefacts is a serious criminal offense. Buy souvenirs only from licensed sellers and keep receipts.
Duty-free allowances for tobacco and alcohol apply per adult; excess quantities must be declared.

payments.text: Cards are accepted in hotels, malls, supermarkets and most restaurants in cities and resorts, but bazaars, small shops, taxis and rural areas run on cash. With high inflation, prices change quickly. Carry some lira and check exchange rates often.

safety.text: Tourist regions of Turkey are generally safe with visible policing. Avoid areas within 10 km of the Syrian border and any demonstrations, and watch for pickpocketing and taxi or restaurant overcharging scams in Istanbul.

bestTimeToVisit.text: April to June and September to October offer warm, dry weather without the peak-summer heat and crowds — ideal for both the coast and inland sights like Cappadocia.

tips.text: Apply for the Turkish eVisa only at the official portal evisa.gov.tr. Look-alike third-party sites charge large markups on the official fee and sometimes deliver nothing.
Taking antiquities or historical artefacts out of Turkey — even stones or coins picked up at a site — is a criminal offense that can lead to arrest at the airport.
Keep small lira notes for taxis, bazaars and tips; card terminals sometimes "fail" in tourist traps to push cash payment at a worse rate.
Insulting the Turkish nation, flag or state institutions (including online) and photographing military sites are criminal offenses. Stay clear of both.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Turkey?
faq.answer: Under the visa exemption introduced in late 2023, US passport holders can visit Turkey visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Because the change is relatively recent, double-check your nationality's status on the official portal evisa.gov.tr shortly before travel.

faq.question: How much does the Turkish eVisa cost?
faq.answer: For nationalities that still need one, the official eVisa costs roughly 50 USD, though the exact fee varies by nationality and is displayed on evisa.gov.tr before payment. It is typically valid for 180 days from the travel date, with stays of 30 or 90 days depending on nationality.

faq.question: How long can EU citizens stay in Turkey without a visa?
faq.answer: Citizens of Germany, France, Spain, Italy and most other European countries can stay visa-free for up to 90 days within any 180-day period. The stay is not extendable as a tourist — longer stays require a short-term residence permit.

faq.question: How long must my passport be valid to enter Turkey?
faq.answer: Turkey asks for a passport valid at least 60 days beyond the end of your permitted stay, but at least 6 months' validity on arrival is recommended, since airlines and border officers often apply the stricter standard.

faq.question: What is Turkey's conditional eVisa?
faq.answer: Certain nationalities (including India, Pakistan, the Philippines and Vietnam) can get a single-entry, 30-day Turkish eVisa only if they hold a valid visa or residence permit from a Schengen country, the US, the UK or Ireland and meet other conditions such as arriving with an approved carrier. Travelers who do not qualify must apply at a Turkish embassy. Eligibility is checked at evisa.gov.tr.
